- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (e.g., -1.0) within 3–5 days, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 5–10 days.
- When model forecasts are consistently above true values (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it; adjust downward by 3–7% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–3% lag correction to forecast for 3–5 days ahead.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) for 3+ days, model often underestimates; add 1–4% upward bias for next 5–7 days.
